review_candidates.description: Position Overview The COO manages HRHA’s daily operations, supports and acts for the CEO, and oversees housing programs, projects, compliance, finances, contracts, and staff. The position also serves as EIV Coordinator, Section 504 Coordinator, and agency Hearing Officer. Key Responsibilities • Oversee 256 public housing units and 611 Housing Choice Vouchers, including occupancy, leasing, rent collection, inspections, recertifications, resident services, and complaints. • Monitor PHAS and SEMAP performance, HUD reporting, capital funds, budgets, utilization, reserves, fees, and monthly financial results. • Manage agency projects, consultants, contractors, service contracts, schedules, budgets, and resources. • Ensure compliance with HUD rules, fair housing and accessibility laws, HRHA policies, and recordkeeping requirements. • Conduct applicant and participant reviews or hearings and manage accommodation, accessibility, and transfer requests. • Build partnerships with landlords, police, schools, social services, and other community organizations. • Produce program reports in Encompass and perform other assigned duties. Operational and Program Oversight The COO is responsible for keeping housing operations eEicient, compliant, and responsive. For Public Housing, this includes monitoring rent collection, occupancy, leasing, work orders, resident counseling, complaint resolution, and compliance with HUD physical condition standards. For the Housing Choice Voucher program, the COO tracks voucher use, annual and interim recertifications, housing quality inspections, and required participant records. The COO reviews performance under the Public Housing Assessment System and the Section Eight Management Assessment Program, identifies weaknesses, and directs corrective action when needed. The position also coordinates agency projects from approval through completion. This includes developing schedules, monitoring budgets, assigning staE and other resources, working with consultants and contractors, and maintaining project information in Basecamp. Service contracts must be reviewed for quality, adherence to specifications, timely renewal, and value to the agency. Compliance, Finance, and Resident Service The COO implements required HUD policies and confirms that programs meet federal reporting and recordkeeping standards. Financial oversight includes forecasting annual funding, reviewing monthly results, comparing actual costs with approved budgets, and monitoring program utilization, reserves, administrative fees, and capital fund spending. The COO audits leasing and occupancy files, documents findings, and follows up on needed corrections. As Section 504 Coordinator, the COO manages reasonable accommodation and transfer requests, evaluates accessibility needs, and updates the agency transition plan. As Hearing OEicer, the COO conducts informal reviews and hearings when applicants or participants challenge an agency decision, ensuring that the process is fair, consistent, and properly documented. The role also maintains working relationships with landlords, law enforcement, schools, social service agencies, and community organizations that support residents and program participants. Supervisory Responsibilities Supervises Public Housing, Housing Choice Voucher, and Project-Based Voucher staff. Duties include hiring, training, assigning work, evaluating performance, and addressing conduct and complaints, and resolving workplace problems. Leadership Expectations The COO sets clear expectations, delegates work appropriately, monitors results, and gives employees timely feedback. The role requires dependable follow-through, sound judgment, ethical conduct, and the ability to solve problems before they disrupt service. The COO should communicate clearly, listen carefully, keep the CEO and staff informed, and respond constructively to questions or concerns. Effective performance also requires teamwork, initiative, adaptability, continued professional development, and a consistent focus on service to residents, participants, colleagues, and community partners. Required Qualifications • Bachelor’s degree in business administration, public administration, or a related field; master’s degree preferred. • Progressively responsible public housing, property management, or Housing Choice Voucher experience, including staff supervision. • Public Housing Manager certification preferred or required within two years; Housing Choice Voucher certification required within the same period. • Knowledge of federal housing rules, civil law, collections, fair housing, disability access laws, and HRHA policies. • Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, planning, teamwork, accountability, initiative, and integrity. • Valid Virginia driver’s license and successful criminal background and drug screenings. Physical Demands and Work Environment The position frequently requires standing, walking, using hands and fingers, bending, stooping, kneeling, or crawling. It occasionally requires sitting and lifting, pushing, or carrying items up to 50 pounds. The employee must also use sufficient visual acuity to operate equipment, read technical information, and use a keyboard.

Serve as KEW's primary finance liaison to Koniag leadership and corporate finance, ensuring alignment on reporting, budgeting, capital planning and governance. Maintain a strong internal control environment and manage external audit relationships. Ensure compliance with ASC 606 revenue recognition requirements. Manage consolidation of Canadian operations, including foreign currency translation, remeasurement and intercompany transactions. Lead annual budgeting, forecasting and cash flow planning. Experience with government contracting, including DCAA-compliant accounting systems, federal cost structures, prevailing wage requirements and certified payroll processes, is highly desirable. Experience overseeing HR and IT functions preferred. Ability to lead distributed teams while maintaining a hands-on approach. CPA and/or MBA required. Candidates who advanced from Controller or Corporate Controller roles into CFO positions are strongly encouraged to apply. Demonstrated experience personally leading ERP implementations, finance system integrations, reporting consolidations, chart-of-account standardization, and post-acquisition finance integration efforts is strongly preferred. Must be comfortable operating in a lean, high-growth environment where the CFO is expected to function as both a strategic leader and an individual contributor when necessary. Finance organization prepared to support future acquisitions and continued growth.
